findings.text: the emitted profile_normalisation.path states the profile column is "the unnormalised observation" because "the operator's moment path resolves moments from the flux directly and ignores the requested current", but the same block's stored numbers refute it: the committed column profile_implied_combination equals the block's normalised_combination bit-for-bit on all six rows and differs from profile_implied_combination_unnormalised by up to +3.45e-2 (combination_shift: −1.11e-3 on 21978/35, +3.45e-2 on 22086/43), and nova/equilibrium/forward.py:1318-1360 rescales moments and support integrals by current_normalisation_amplitude(target_current, …) on exactly this use_linear_moments=False path; the true reason the column could not move is that it is computed by profile.integral_observation(state, target_current) at line 659, which never receives the exchanged ConstraintContext — only the row kernel does, at lines 553-561. The false sentence is quoted verbatim as the reason in docs/evidence/archive/constraint-augmented-newton-krylov-landed.html:481-483, where it sits beside the combination_shift sentence that contradicts it.

commensurability is called with major_radius=shape["major_radius_m"], which _metrics fills from observation.centroid_r (lines 546, 584) — the current centroid — while the same block's nova_radius_convention string (lines 481-485) defines R as nova's volume-weighted sum(radial volume elements)/volume (nova/equilibrium/observation.py:543), the value this receipt already carries as unit_check.major_radius_m and uses in recomputed_profile_moments (line 366); the two differ by 5.9% to 12.6% per row (0.7700 m against 0.8673 m on 21978/35), so nova_major_radius_m, the row JSON's convention_sentence ("against nova's volume-weighted major radius 0.7700 m") and the plan comment's "17% to 27% from nova's volume-weighted major radius" name the wrong baseline and understate every distance: against the true volume-weighted R the implied radius sits 25.2% to 33.9% away, not the stated 17.0% to 26.8%, and row 21986/46's "near-marginal (18.3% against 17.0%)" is an artifact of the centroid baseline — against the volume-weighted radius that row is 25.2% against 27.1%, not marginal.

the plan comment says the two distances differ "by exactly the aspect ratio" and quotes an envelope of "0.4% to 18.3%": the radii differ by the aspect ratio (1.317 to 1.426 per row), not the distances, whose numerators differ; and the recomputed minimum distance from the boundary minor radius is 0.16% (22086/43), so the quoted envelope clips its own floor.

justifications.durability: the arithmetic is pinned by tests/test_shafranov_combination_discriminator.py — the ConstraintContext field order and the driver's named-field construction, the identity round-trip and its refusal cases, boundary_shape, attribute, recomputed_profile_moments, implied_radius including its None guards, commensurability's positive control and its minor-radius negative, and the reading order and labels — all re-run green first-hand (15 passed in 14.15 s); what is not pinned is the committed receipt's own numbers or the receipt-building driver path, so a regression that moved a row's stored combination while leaving the pure functions green would fail no test.
justifications.evidence: every fence check re-ran first-hand — the gate tests/test_shafranov_combination_discriminator.py in one all_debug job on JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu through the shared interpreter (15 passed in 14.15 s, EXIT=0, slurm-gate-1273770.out), the identity equalities recomputed from the receipt's own scalars (magnetics_implied_combination equals the circular identity bit-for-bit on all six rows; the superseded b724321c row-kernel value equals the new constraint_row_reading_unnormalised bit-for-bit on all six, and the corrected reading differs from it by −1.40e−3 to +4.25e−2), the extraction floor reproduced per row (0.2270768, 0.2528019, 0.2927609, 0.1600217, 0.2761531, 0.2274435), and the six SVG digests match the row JSONs; the one softness is that the row-kernel/identity agreement is an equality by construction (the production observed and the driver's copy are the same inversion on the same inputs), so it evidences the context placement rather than an independent magnetics path — which the record itself states accurately.
justifications.fit: the new module sits beside the discriminator it extends, the receipt mirrors the frozen receipt shape with a unit_check block that recomputes nova's own definitions, the panels are drawn through the committed nova.media painters (draw_wall, draw_nulls with DEFAULT_INK, poloidal plotting on the shared levels_wb as unfilled line contours), and are published as SVG beside PNG under the serving mount; the naming checks over the diff are clean and the new identifiers are mechanism-named.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the recomputation is delivered in full — six row documents and the receipt regenerated on the corrected context (389dedb8, 6255587a, 82165c48, 6cf3e19e, ec1d72d2, 7a7b70ed; merged 97460c12), the row kernel equal to the circular identity at the boundary minor radius bit-for-bit on all six rows (row_kernel_versus_circular_residual 0.0), the commensurability question computed rather than asserted, and every row carrying a line-contour terminal-state panel; but the delivered record's two load-bearing explanations misstate their own mechanism — profile_normalisation.path calls the profile column the unnormalised observation and gives an operator behaviour the code contradicts, and the commensurability statement labels the current centroid "nova's volume-weighted major radius" — so the answer the goal asked for is right while two of its stated reasons are wrong.
justifications.scope_discipline: all six commits lie on the discriminator's own surface — the benchmark driver, its test module, the figure receipts and state panels, the landed evidence record, and one plan comment (6 inserted lines) — no nova package code is touched, the plan-version meta line is not moved (7a7b70ed changes only a comment body, six lines), and every commit carries a body with no AI attribution.

CHECKS (the evidence behind the scores; no other prefixed lines follow)
gate: tests/test_shafranov_combination_discriminator.py re-ran first-hand in one all_debug job (1273770, 4 CPUs, 64G, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu, the root .venv interpreter with PYTHONPATH at the reviewed tree, no uv on the node): 15 passed in 14.15 s, EXIT=0, log slurm-gate-1273770.out in the review run directory.
receipt: regenerated receipt.json read directly; rows_receipt carries six full row documents with identity, the five readings, unit_check, commensurability, the two normalisation blocks, the round-trip residuals and the state panel block; row_kernel_versus_circular_residual is 0.0 on all six and magnetics_implied_combination reproduces the circular identity recomputed from the receipt's own stored scalars, equal in IEEE double on every row.
superseded: the b724321c receipt's magnetics_implied_combination equals the new constraint_row_reading_unnormalised bit-for-bit on all six rows (0.31245935764258936, 0.32367449413917804, 0.4797315370890942, 0.322343104260131, 0.49121359468124637, 0.28166321417628093), so the argument-order fix moved the headline magnetics reading by −1.40e−3 to +4.25e−2 and the profile column by exactly zero.
profile column: bit-identical old against new on all six rows; the committed value equals the block's normalised_combination, and the nonzero combination_shift (up to +3.45e-2) is what refutes the unnormalised path label.
commensurability: implied radii recomputed from the stored scalars and reproduced bit-exact (r_beta 0.582308144310385 and r_li 0.5801835837000869 on 21978/35; the two agree to 0.36% to 4.94% per row, inside the stated 5%); the implied radius sits 0.16% to 18.33% from each row's boundary minor radius, 17.01% to 26.84% from the centroid, and 25.21% to 33.91% from nova's volume-weighted major radius — so the denominator convention is a minor-radius-scale radius, near but not exactly the boundary minor radius, and the receipt's own radius label is the wrong one of the two it stores.
panels: all six state SVGs read as text (no PNG was opened): twelve unfilled line contours per panel at the stored levels_wb with fill: none, one black wall polyline, and two null markers — the axis (filled dot) and one admitted X-point (filled cross) — matching each row's stored topology (read_status qualified, class 1); the manifest's stated deviation that only one null set is drawn is confirmed and immaterial, because a panel carries a single field with no reference beside it, so there is no second set to draw.
digests: sha256 of each of the six state SVGs equals the digest recorded in its row JSON.
commits: all six commits carry bodies, carry no AI attribution, and touch only the benchmark driver, its test module, the figure directory, the landed evidence record and one plan comment.
follow-on (outside this node): the panels draw the axis as the committed style's dot (nova/media/ink.py:76 axis_marker=".") and the X-point as its cross (ink.py:79), while the plotting ruling's prose describes a solid triangle for the axis; the node used the committed painters as instructed, so the divergence is between nova.media's own default vocabulary and the ruling text, not a defect of this landing.
